findings.title: Qualified release identity
findings.detail: A detached v0.6.2 checkout supplied unchanged application sources, assets and build configuration. Only the capture harness/container mount was added outside application source.

findings.title: Explicit synthetic scenarios
findings.detail: A fixed finished local game and a public emulator fixture provide repeatable content. No real account or private production data was used.

findings.title: Human and physical-device acceptance
findings.detail: These are headless Chromium viewport references. They do not establish physical touch, browser-chrome, screen-reader or new visual acceptance.

technical: Captured 2026-10-24T23:16:11.102Z in chromium 156.0.8078.4, DPR 1, reduced motion.
Application source tree fcfe58b5924011ec78e053f64e8ea5a594e7563d; release source 37a122d2bd8e899bcfc581055e685c0327f43cb4.
The capture run completed all 24 requested viewport/scale images. This curated record selects 18 images for six core surfaces and relevant stress cases.
The isolated emulator used offset 1000 and demo-gomoku2d-acceptance. Existing manual preview/emulators and public demo were untouched.
Renderer preference was AUTO; the actual per-capture renderer was not observed. These images qualify layout rather than engine pixel behavior.

The public fixture carries the publisher UID in its replay participant; the harness asserts visible opponent metadata before capture. Initial fixture/locator corrections remain in the local execution log.
human: Bryan reviewed earlier sharing/profile work during 0.6.1/0.6.2. This newly prepared reference set has not received a separate human or physical-device pass.
followUp: Keep this release reference frozen. New application captures should form a new dated record with their own source/fixture identity; historical review pairs retain their original meaning.

title: A consistent family of action icons
question: Can publishing and account actions read clearly beside the existing pixel icons?
summary: Publish, Sign in/out, Trash, Sync and Exit retain the established 24px rectangle language. Cloud remains deferred.

comparisons.title: Reference family and retained additions
comparisons.conditions: Asset renders, not before/after application captures. Original 24px SVGs at native/integer enlarged sizes. Browser/capture timestamp was not recorded in this historical artifact.

findings.title: Distinct publishing and account actions
findings.detail: Publish replaces the ambiguous Profile glyph. Account arrows share one frame; Trash and Sync have explicit roles.

findings.title: Cloud shape
findings.detail: Cloud did not meet visual acceptance and was removed. No new quit action was added for the available Exit icon.

technical: Recorded geometry/raster checks cover integer coordinates, bounds and source derivations.
Original review recorded exact 1×/2×/10× raster comparisons and 320px reflow. Asset availability does not establish runtime usage.
human: Bryan selected Publish, the account pair and power-style Exit, then requested retaining the accepted icons and cutting Cloud. Physical-device acceptance was not recorded for this artifact.
followUp: Canonical icons remain inspectable in Design & assets. Historical pixels stay frozen; later source changes must become a new record.

title: Keep mobile records within reach
scope: 0.6.2 / Profile, public player and landscape match
question: Can useful controls and records stay reachable on a narrow or short screen?
summary: A compact Profile header, stable record tabs and clearer public replay rows reduce repeated chrome. This is an intermediate historical checkpoint.

technical: The original checkpoint records 504 unit checks, affected browser journeys and offset-1000 emulator validation. Counts qualify that checkpoint only.
Source PNG hashes and dimensions are retained; Profile/Public player pairs use matching scenarios. Other saved-game captures with different session timestamps were not selected for this pair.

followUp: Later landscape/enlarged-text fixes landed at 9c4c3bb. The 0.6.2 release record supersedes this checkpoint for publication and final automated results.

title: A public player page with a useful record
question: How can a public player page feel like part of the game and expose meaningful data?
summary: A two-column record view keeps identity and link controls on the left, optional statistics and a paged replay list on the right. These are dated implementation captures, not the initial mockup.

comparisons.title: Desktop and portrait at the same checkpoint
comparisons.conditions: Synthetic public fixture, 18 replay rows. Desktop and portrait are different viewport conditions, not a before/after claim. Browser and text-scale details are retained in original evidence where available.

findings.title: More useful hierarchy
findings.detail: Public name, existing replay count and link controls form a compact identity panel. Statistics remain optional and self-reported.

findings.title: A bounded catalog, without a new public field
findings.detail: The view keeps existing public data and paged replay semantics. Presentation changes do not add cloud operations.

technical: Original implementation evidence records route, responsive and catalog/error-state checks.
The later mobile checkpoint and release record contain follow-up results; these captures keep their original source identity.
human: Bryan chose the record-style direction with two columns and requested more substance on the left. Later mobile feedback was broadly positive; physical-phone acceptance remains separate.
followUp: Follow the mobile-records review for responsive refinements and the release record for shipped source/results.
